    "title": "The chromatic-plus-one conjecture for additive coloring",
    "statement": "Let $G$ be a graph. Write $\\chi(G)$ for its chromatic number. The conjecture is presented as an open problem.",

  "322978": {
    "mathdb_id": 322978,
    "title": "The distinct-neighborhood antimagic labeling conjecture",
    "statement": "Let $G$ be a simple graph on $n$ vertices, and let $N(v)$ denote the neighborhood of a vertex $v$. Assume that no two vertices have the same neighborhood.\n\n**Distinct-neighborhood antimagic labeling conjecture.** There is a bijection $f:V(G)\\rightarrow \\{1,2,\\ldots,n\\}$ such that\n\n$$\n\\sum_{x\\in N(u)}f(x)\\neq\\sum_{x\\in N(v)}f(x)\n$$\n\nfor any two distinct vertices $u$ and $v$.\n\nThis is introduced as a vertex analogue of the antimagic labeling conjecture of Ringel. The paper gives no resolution, so the problem remains open.",

    "title": "Hamilton decomposition conjecture for regular tripartite tournaments",
    "statement": "A **tripartite tournament** is an orientation of a complete tripartite graph. It is **regular** when all vertex classes have equal size and every vertex has equal indegree and outdegree. A Hamilton decomposition is a decomposition of its arcs into directed Hamilton cycles.\n\n**Tripartite tournament conjecture.** Every regular tripartite tournament has a Hamilton decomposition.\n\nThe paper proves the corresponding result for regular $k$-partite tournaments with $k\\ge 4$ and explicitly conjectures that it extends to all $k\\ge 2$. The tripartite case is therefore the first unresolved case beyond the proven range.",

    "title": "Closed-form enumeration conjecture for maximal dominant weights of affine sl(n)-modules",
    "statement": "Let $V(k\\Lambda_0)$ be the integrable highest weight $\\widehat{sl}(n)$-module, with $n\\geq 2$ and $k\\geq 1$. A maximal dominant weight is a dominant weight in $V(k\\Lambda_0)$ that is maximal with respect to subtraction of positive roots.\n\n**Enumeration conjecture.** For fixed $n\\geq 2$, the number of maximal dominant weights of $V(k\\Lambda_0)$ is\n\n$$\n\\frac{1}{n+k}\\sum_{d\\mid\\gcd(n,k)}\\phi(d)\\binom{(n+k)/d}{k/d},\n$$\n\nwhere $\\phi$ is the Euler phi function.\n\nThe formula gives a closed-form count for the maximal dominant weights. The source states that it is proved for $k\\leq 3$, while the general case is presented as a conjecture.",

    "mathdb_id": 326586,
    "title": "Caputo's shuffle spectral gap conjecture",
    "statement": "Let $n$ be a positive integer with $n\\ge 3$. For each $A\\subset\\{1,\\ldots,n\\}$, let $S_{n,A}$ be the set of permutations in $S_n$ fixing every element outside $A$, and define\n\n$$\nJ_{n,A}:=\\sum_{\\pi\\in S_{n,A}}\\pi.\n$$\n\nFor nonnegative coefficients $\\alpha_A$, set\n\n$$\nw=\\sum_{A\\subset\\{1,\\ldots,n\\}}\\alpha_AJ_{n,A}.\n$$\n\nLet $\\operatorname{supp}w$ denote the support of $w$, and let $\\psi_{S_n}(w)$ be the spectral gap of $w$, while $\\psi_{S_n}(w,\\mathsf D)$ is the spectral gap in the representation $\\mathsf D$. **Caputo's conjecture.** If $\\operatorname{supp}w$ generates $S_n$, then\n\n$$\n\\psi_{S_n}(w)=\\psi_{S_n}(w,\\mathsf D).\n$$\n\nThis conjecture was communicated privately by P. Caputo, and the source reports that it resisted both proof attempts and numerical disproof; no resolution is supplied.",

    "title": "Elekes's uniform statistical conjecture for small image sets of lines",
    "statement": "Let $\\mathcal{L}$ denote the set of lines under consideration.
